Marissa — thanks for the recap and the diagram. A few quick clarifications from the security team: 

1) Egress: our policy is that any external egress from the VPC must be approved and go through our egress proxy/NAT with strict allow lists. Will Redwood require outbound connections to external services (model telemetry, updates, licensing)? If so, can those be restricted to IPs we control?

2) Model updates & air-gap: we need to understand whether Redwood can support an offline model sync process (transfer via signed package and customer appliance) rather than pulling from the internet.

3) Logging: we prefer that audit logs (request/response metadata) can be streamed to our SIEM (Splunk) over TLS and that PII payloads are not retained by default. Can you confirm retention minimums and whether we can set retention to zero for raw payloads?

Security team also attached a short questionnaire (acme_security_questionnaire.xlsx) — we'll need answers from your infra/security team before we schedule a full workshop.

Hi Alex — thanks for the clear questions. Short answers below plus details: 

1) Egress & outbound connections:
- Redwood Private can be deployed inside your VPC with no mandatory outbound calls — the runtime itself does not require a persistent internet connection to serve inference requests.
- Optional features (telemetry, usage reporting, automated model updates) can be configured to use an outbound path, but they are not required. If enabled, we can restrict outbound endpoints to a narrow IP range or FQDNs; for stricter controls we support routing outbound through your NAT/proxy with mTLS.

2) Air-gapped / offline model sync:
- We support an offline model sync process: Redwood can deliver signed model artifacts and an installer bundle. Customers can ingest these via a secure appliance or direct import into the private environment.
- We provide a checksum and signature verification process; for highly regulated deployments we offer an on-prem sync appliance (usb/hardware transfer is allowed per your process) and a one-time activation token.

3) Logging & retention:
- Audit logs (request metadata, timestamps, model version, latency, token counts) can be streamed to your SIEM (Splunk/ELK) over TLS.
- By default we do not persist raw PII payloads beyond the configured retention window. You can configure payload retention to 0 (no persisted raw payloads) while keeping metadata/audit logs as needed.
- Key management: Redwood Private supports customer-managed keys via KMS/HSM; secrets never leave your control plane in that configuration.

Security/compliance docs: we have a SOC 2 report and can share a redacted copy under an NDA. I attached a short one-page note on retention and KMS integration.

Let us know the questions from the questionnaire we should prioritize for the workshop. Happy to run a 60–90 minute technical session with your infra and security leads.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
